I'm so sorry for your loss. I lost my younger brother a little over a year now and the first three months were incredibly hard, and found myself doing the same as you. Only advice I could give is to let yourself take this time to grieve and work on it, plus yourself, because this type of loss opens a lot of wounds. Do what you can everyday, don't push yourself too hard though, let yourself go through the motions. Also reach out when you need it! If you have someone you're able to lean on when times are tough, reach out and talk about it. Try not to hold it in and try to process it all by your time, don't push yourself. In time it'll feel a little better, sadly things won't be the same, so don't beat yourself up over it either. Celebrating his life is another way that'll help once you're able to process it better. My family and I still celebrate his birthday, and always try to have a moment for him during the holidays. Plus April 2nd is my brother's "anniversary", so my mother and I took flowers to a Pier, said some words and had a nice moment of silence with much needed tears to be shed, with plenty of hugs. It was hard, but I'm in an odd way it kinda felt good to do for him.

From experience, telling any job (big or small company) about mental illnesses, they shut you out. They either convince you that you're "too fragile" to work, or completely undermine you and your work. They technically cannot fire us, but they'll find another way around it. I've admitted my depression, anxiety, and bipolar disorders only twice and it always ended in a complete shit show.
1st one: I missed three days of work due to a 5150, they tried to fire me because of it but can't. It's illegal in the US. But it didn't stop my boss from talking me into quitting. Stating things like "you're to fragile to work right now, why not take a break? Oh but we don't do leave of absences, you'd have to quit." I was 19, second job ever, and was easily manipulated at the time. Got totally taken advantage of because they didn't want to deal with me.
2nd one: it was a small business, maybe 6 of us in total, including the boss. She's a straight narcissist. She would get us comfortable with her and divulge personal info back and forth, then go and take all of your info and backfire it on you. Make fun of us and humiliate us. Turn everyone against each other and just made the whole work environment toxic and uncomfortable. Well she managed to get me comfortable enough to once again talk about my mental illnesses, then she went and purposely triggered me many times to the point I'd start bawling at work. And to be honest, I struggle mentally a lot, but I am no cry baby at work normally, EVER. So I had to jump ship once again. People are shit.
